Claim:
That a federal judge “ordered President Donald Trump” to restore CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s White House press access.
Began: Sep 24, 2026 | Ended: No ending date (live as of Sep 24, 2026)
Deception_Form: misstatement of court order (who was ordered)
Notes: Temporary restraining order, ¶2: “Defendants (except for President Trump) and their agents, representatives, and all persons or entities acting in concert with them shall immediately return, reinstate, and restore the White House ‘hard pass’ press credentials…” The court expressly left the President out of the order. The substance of the story (the administration was ordered to restore access) is accurate; the error is naming Trump personally as the person ordered. Severity: low/technical, but the order's text directly contradicts it. ABC News (US) got it right: “The order requires the defendants, excluding President Donald Trump…” (https://abcnews.com/US/judge-orders-white-house-restore-press-passes-cnn/story?id=136709442). Same family of error as NEW-2026-09-24-02; merge them if you catalog this as one case.
speaker: Callum Sutherland and Olivia-Anne Cleary
exact_quote: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico reporters were allowed back into the White House Thursday after a federal judge ordered President Donald Trump to immediately restore their press access.
record_shows: The TRO (ECF 24, Sep 24, 2026) orders “Defendants (except for President Trump)” and their agents to restore the hard passes. The President is expressly carved out.

Claim:
That a US judge “ordered Donald Trump” to restore White House access for CNN, Politico and MS NOW.
Began: Sep 24, 2026 | Ended: No ending date (live as of Sep 24, 2026)
Who_Pushed_It: ABC News (Australia), Rudi Maxwell with wires (Reuters/ABC)
Deception_Form: misstatement of court order (who was ordered), in the headline
Notes: The headline reads “Judge orders Donald Trump to restore White House access to banned media organisations,” and the summary says “A US judge has ordered Donald Trump to restore access…” The order's operative paragraph excludes President Trump. The story is marked Reuters/ABC, but I could not verify whether Reuters' own copy uses the same wording, so this entry is attributed to ABC Australia only. Severity: low/technical. Merge with NEW-2026-09-24-01 if cataloged as one case.
speaker: Rudi Maxwell (with wires)
exact_quote: A US judge has ordered Donald Trump to restore access to the White House for three media outlets he had banned: CNN, Politico and MS Now.
record_shows: TRO ¶2 binds “Defendants (except for President Trump)” and their agents. It is not directed at Trump personally.

Claim:
That Trump “barred the Associated Press from the White House” in 2025 (Gulf of America dispute), presented as a precedent for the 2026 total ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
Began: Sep 23, 2026 (this instance) | Ended: No ending date (live as of Sep 24, 2026)
Who_Pushed_It: NPR (David Folkenflik), syndicated by GPB (Morning Edition)
Deception_Form: overstatement / omitted context (scope of the AP restriction)
Notes: In AP v. Budowich (D.D.C., Apr. 8, 2025, ECF 46, p.9), Judge McFadden wrote: “The parties agree that no AP employee's hard pass has been revoked” (see also p.12: “both parties agreed that the AP's hard pass status had been unchanged”). The AP was kept out of the press pool, the Oval Office, Air Force One and many East Room events. It was not barred from the White House. The 2026 ban is different: it revoked hard passes and blocked access to the whole complex. Saying the AP was “barred from the White House” leaves out that the AP kept its hard passes and general access to the press facilities, which makes the 2025 action look like the 2026 one. Labeled misleading rather than false because “barred” is partly true for specific events. I found no fact-check on this line.
speaker: David Folkenflik
exact_quote: Trump barred the Associated Press from the White House last year, after he deemed the Gulf of Mexico should be called the Gulf of America, but the news wire declined to follow suit.
record_shows: The court record in AP v. Budowich says no AP hard pass was revoked. The restriction covered the pool, the Oval Office, Air Force One and many limited-access events, not the White House itself.
proof_type: Official record (court opinion; key fact omitted)
dedupe_status: NEW. No AP-access case in the catalog
